This walkthrough runs the everyday loop from the terminal: initialize a project,
add a file and commit its metadata to git, check its status, delete it, then get
it back. It is the "I re-cloned a project and need its data" sequence. The
[R walkthrough](getting-started.html) covers the same steps from R.

## Setup

R creates the sandbox directories and the dataset; all dvs operations run via
the `dvs` binary.

```{r}
#| message: false
options(width = 1000)
library(here)
storage     <- basename(tempfile(fileext = "_storage"))
new_project <- basename(tempfile(fileext = "_project"))
dir.create(here::here(storage))
dir.create(here::here(new_project))
dir.create(here::here(new_project, "data"))
write.csv(Theoph, here::here(new_project, "data/theoph.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
Sys.setenv(DVS_PROJECT = here::here(new_project), DVS_STORAGE = here::here(storage))
```

## 1. Initialize

Point storage at the sibling directory. See [dvs init](cli-init.html) for every
flag.

Make the project folder a git repository too, before the first add.

```{bash}
cd "$DVS_PROJECT"
git init --quiet --initial-branch=main
dvs init local "$DVS_STORAGE"
```

```{bash}
#| include: false
# The rendered page commits as a placeholder user. Yours is your git config.
cd "$DVS_PROJECT"
git config user.name "dvs docs"
git config user.email "docs@example.com"
```

::: {.callout-important}
dvs keeps the data out of git with `.gitignore` entries that it writes during
`dvs add`, and only when the project folder itself holds the `.git` folder. A
dvs project in a subfolder of a git repository gets no entries, and neither
does a file added before `git init`. git then sees the data. Before your first
commit, check what git would commit, as in step 2.
:::

## 2. Add and commit

Track the CSV with a message. See [dvs add](cli-add.html).

```{bash}
cd "$DVS_PROJECT"
dvs add data/theoph.csv -m "initial Theoph data"
```

List what git would commit. `--untracked-files=all` lists the files inside new
folders. Plain `git status` shows only the folders `data/` and `.dvs/`, which
looks as if the data would be committed.

```{bash}
cd "$DVS_PROJECT"
git status --short --untracked-files=all
```

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `dvs.toml` | The project configuration: where the storage is. |
| `.dvs/data/theoph.csv.dvs` | The meta file: hash, size, who added the file, when, and the message. |
| `data/.gitignore` | The entry `/theoph.csv`, which keeps the data out of git. |
| `.dvs/.gitignore` | The entry `/.cache`, which keeps dvs's local cache out of git. |

`data/theoph.csv` is not in the list. `git check-ignore -v` names the line that
ignores it:

```{bash}
cd "$DVS_PROJECT"
git check-ignore -v data/theoph.csv
```

Commit. If git has no name and email for you yet, the commit stops and asks.
Set them once, with `git config --global user.name "Your Name"` and
`git config --global user.email "you@example.com"`.

```{bash}
cd "$DVS_PROJECT"
git add -A
git commit --quiet -m "Track data/theoph.csv with dvs"
git show --name-only --format=%s HEAD
```

Commit the meta file each time you add or update data, and push it. A clone
knows only the meta files that were committed. In a colleague's clone, a file
whose meta file you did not commit is "not tracked by dvs".

## 3. Status

The file is tracked and `current`. See [dvs status](cli-status.html).

```{bash}
cd "$DVS_PROJECT"
dvs status
```

## 4. Remove the file

Delete the local copy, the moment after a fresh clone where the data is not on
disk yet.

```{bash}
cd "$DVS_PROJECT"
rm data/theoph.csv
```

## 5. Status again

The file is now `absent`: tracked, but missing locally.

```{bash}
cd "$DVS_PROJECT"
dvs status
```

::: {.callout-note}
dvs reports five statuses: `current`, `absent`, `stale` (unchanged since dvs
wrote it, while the tracked version moved on), `modified` (edited locally) and
`unsynced` (different, with no record of what dvs wrote). See
[dvs status](cli-status.html) and [Storage and meta files](intro-internals.html).
:::

## 6. Get

Restore the file from storage. See [dvs get](cli-get.html).

```{bash}
cd "$DVS_PROJECT"
dvs get data/theoph.csv
```

## 7. Status again

The file is `current` again. The loop is complete.

```{bash}
cd "$DVS_PROJECT"
dvs status
```

## Cleanup

```{r}
unlink(here::here(new_project), recursive = TRUE)
unlink(here::here(storage),     recursive = TRUE)
```
